notes:
Check first:
1. Bare Latin epithets (alba n35, arborea n70, arboreus n71, cinerea n344, campestris n281, auratus n87, arvensis n80): each depends on the genus printed before it. n70 and n344 have 14-17 observations, and arborea/arboreus can mean Tree Pipit or Woodlark.
2. n6 and n30 (A./Alauda arboreus): I chose Tree Pipit for the spring rush and Woodlark for 29 October.
3. 'Barnacle' (n96, n102; 150+ observations): keepers sometimes use it for any wild goose. n101 has a committee note that the specimen was a White-fronted Goose, so I mapped it to that.
4. Garbled headings I decoded: ALAUDIDÆ (n81-82), ALCIDÆ (n84-85), ANTHIDÆ (n62, n69), BLACKCAP (n261), BLACK REDSTART (n257), BLUE TIT (n269), CHOUGH (n336). Still unread: n133, n198, n348, n18, n13, n4, n108, n115.
5. Keeper names that are probable but not certain: 'sepoys' (n1, read as sea-pyes = Oystercatcher), Black Duck/Scoter (n151-152, n165-167, all Common Scoter), Black Martin/Swallow (n160, n168-169, Swift), Books (n240, OCR for Rooks), Black-headed Bunting (n195, which I mapped to Reed Bunting because of the 18 March date), C. graculus (n275, mapped to Shag).
6. Unresolved local names: Black Diver (n149-150), Blue Janet (n215-216), Chit-chat (n333-334), Black-footed Petrel (n192-193).

Decisions you may want to change:
- Victorian 'hawk' covers both Accipitridae and Falconidae, which aren't one modern family. So for unnamed hawks (n158, n252-253) I used level group, 'hawks (birds of prey)', rather than the family level your examples suggested.
- Bean Goose (n17, n109-110) is at genus Anser, because IOC splits it into Taiga and Tundra.
- Victorian genera Anas, Alauda and Charadrius were broader than today's, so n45, n28 and n320 are at family level.
- 'Anthidæ' (n61) is genus Anthus, the pipits.
- Boatswain/Chaser names are genus Stercorarius (usually Arctic Skua).
- 'Brown Owl' (n255) is at family Strigidae, because one offshore in May is more likely Short-eared than Tawny.
- IOC English names are used throughout. British names, where different, are in the notes: Long-tailed Jaeger is Long-tailed Skua; Black-throated Loon is Black-throated Diver; Common Murre is Guillemot.
- Whitethroat and Barred Warbler are in Curruca, following the current IOC list.
- Black Swan (n170) and Carrier Pigeons (n291-292) are escapes or domestic birds. You may want to exclude them.
